headline: Nepal Oil Corporation Holds Fuel Prices Steady, Says It Will Lose Rs 3.2 Billion
dek: NOC puts the cost of one 15 day pricing cycle at Rs 3.2 billion but has not said whether its rainy day fund covers any of it.
body_markdown:
Nepal Oil Corporation, the state company that imports and sells all petrol, diesel and cooking gas in the country, decided on Wednesday, September 30, to leave retail fuel prices unchanged even though its supplier raised its own rate. Indian Oil Corporation sent a new price list that day lifting petrol by Rs 20.44 a litre and diesel by Rs 20.21 a litre, Setopati and Nepal Press reported.

For now, that means the price you pay at the pump does not move, right before Dashain, the year's biggest travel and shopping season. NOC said the freeze will cost the corporation itself an estimated Rs 3.2 billion over the next 15 days, according to its own statement reported by Nepal Press. That is about $24 million at Nepal Rastra Bank's rate of Rs 133.50 a dollar on September 30, 2026.

NOC cited two reasons for absorbing the hit rather than passing it on: the extraordinary floods and landslides that hit the Bhotekoshi area, and the approaching Dashain festival, OnlineKhabar English reported. NOC also did not raise kerosene prices, which Nepal Press reported IOC had increased by Rs 15.96 a litre.

Nepal is supposed to run fuel pricing on an "automatic pricing mechanism" under which NOC adjusts retail prices every 15 days to match whatever IOC sends, without a board vote. But that formula has not always run automatically. NOC revived the mechanism in July 2023 after it had sat "defunct for nine years," the Kathmandu Post reported. It lasted barely three months. After then prime minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal ordered a rollback of a cooking gas price rise on October 1, 2023, Manoj Kumar Thakur, then an NOC deputy director, told the Kathmandu Post that "the implementation of the auto-pricing mechanism has been halted since then." Wednesday's decision was taken by NOC's board, Ekantipur reported.

## What the coverage missed

The Setopati and Nepal Press reports on the freeze did not mention that NOC's deputy director told the Kathmandu Post in November 2023 that automatic pricing had been halted. That discretion has now been used twice to block price rises the formula would have required. The first was in 2023, when a prime minister ordered a cooking gas rollback. The second is now, for Dashain.

Those two reports also did not mention NOC's Price Stabilization Fund, a reserve built from a levy NOC charges on every litre it sells for exactly this kind of shock, according to the Samriddhi Foundation's study of the fund. On March 4, 2026, Thakur, by then named by the Kathmandu Post as NOC's spokesperson, told the paper the fund held "nearly Rs 20 billion." That is about $150 million at the same rate. That figure is seven months old. It predates the Gulf crisis fuel losses that followed. Clickmandu reported NOC's losses reached Rs 18.81 billion by early April. NOC has not said what the fund holds now. Its statement on the freeze presented the Rs 3.2 billion as a loss and did not say whether the fund was drawn on.

NOC's own published board list gives the chairman's seat to the government's Secretary of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies. Economist Nepal reported in 2023 that Madhukumar Marasini held that role and chaired NOC's board. That means the body approving a price freeze timed for the festival is chaired by a sitting government official.

## What we still do not know

Whether NOC drew on its Price Stabilization Fund this time, and what the fund's current balance is, a question for NOC's finance department or the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies.

How long the freeze will last, and whether NOC plans a sharper price correction once Dashain ends, a question for NOC's board or spokesperson.

How the Rs 3.2 billion figure compares with NOC's audited accounts rather than its own press statement, a question for the Office of the Auditor General or NOC's audited financial reports.

Whether households and transporters in flood hit Bhotekoshi, the area NOC cited as a reason for the freeze, were consulted, a question for local district offices or transport associations there.

key_facts.fact: Indian Oil Corporation raised its supply price by Rs 20.44 a litre for petrol and Rs 20.21 for diesel on September 30, 2026.

Nepal Oil Corporation estimates its decision to hold retail prices steady will cost the corporation Rs 3.2 billion, about $24 million at Nepal Rastra Bank's rate of Rs 133.50 a dollar, over one 15 day pricing cycle.
NOC cited the floods and landslides in the Bhotekoshi area and the approaching Dashain festival as reasons for the freeze.

NOC's automatic pricing mechanism, revived in July 2023 after being defunct for nine years, was halted within three months after a prime ministerial order to roll back a cooking gas price rise, NOC deputy director Manoj Kumar Thakur said at the time.

NOC's price stabilization fund, built from a levy on every litre of fuel sold, held nearly Rs 20 billion, about $150 million at the same rate, as of March 4, 2026, according to NOC spokesperson Thakur. That figure predates the Gulf crisis fuel losses that followed.
NOC reported cumulative losses of Rs 18.81 billion by early April 2026 during the Gulf crisis fuel shock.

NOC's published board list names the government's Secretary of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies as the corporation's board chairman, a role held by Madhukumar Marasini when reported in 2023.

social_hook: Your petrol price did not rise this week only because Nepal Oil Corporation chose to absorb what it estimates is a Rs 3.2 billion hit instead of passing India's hike to you before Dashain.
take: Nepal Oil Corporation did not raise fuel prices before Dashain, and every household filling a tank this week benefits from that call. But its own record complicates the good news. The company's "automatic" pricing formula stopped being automatic within months of its 2023 revival, after a prime minister ordered a rollback, NOC's own deputy director said at the time. NOC has also not said whether its price stabilization fund, reported near Rs 20 billion in March, before the Gulf crisis losses that followed, covered any of this freeze. Readers deserve that accounting before the next price cycle.

caption.hook: Your petrol and diesel price did not move, days before Dashain. Indian Oil raised its rate over Rs 20 a litre. NOC says it is eating the gap.
caption.body:
Nepal Oil Corporation decided on Wednesday, September 30, to leave petrol and diesel prices unchanged. Indian Oil Corporation had just raised its own petrol rate by Rs 20.44 a litre. Diesel rose by Rs 20.21 a litre.

NOC cited the floods and landslides in Bhotekoshi, and the approaching Dashain festival. NOC estimates the freeze will cost it Rs 3.2 billion. That covers one 15 day pricing cycle, Nepal Press reported.

That means your fuel bill stays flat through the festival, for now. NOC has not said how long the freeze will last, or whether prices jump once Dashain ends.

NOC has a price stabilization fund built for shocks like this. It held nearly Rs 20 billion in March, the Kathmandu Post reported. That was before the Gulf crisis losses. NOC has not said if this freeze used it. NOC's deputy director said in November 2023 that automatic pricing had been halted. A prime minister had ordered a gas price rollback.
caption.trigger: Would you rather NOC spend its rainy day fund to keep fuel flat through Dashain, or save it and pass the price rise on now?

angles.claim: Nepal's fuel pricing is supposed to run on an 'Automatic Pricing Mechanism' that forces NOC to adjust retail prices every 15 days strictly on the basis of the tariff IOC sends — removing board discretion — yet the board has repeatedly chosen not to follow the formula, including when it required a price cut, not just now when it requires a hike.
angles.why_it_matters: If the 'automatic' mechanism is actually discretionary whenever it is politically convenient, then today's framing of the freeze as an emergency response to floods and Dashain hides a longer pattern of the board overriding its own rulebook — which matters for whether Nepalis can trust that prices will also come down automatically when IOC's rate falls.

evidence.fact: The NOC board decided not to pass on a Rs 27.44 per cylinder LPG price decrease that the IOC tariff called for, 'citing a loss of Rs296.15 in a cooking gas cylinder.'
Nepal Oil Corporation's automatic fuel pricing mechanism, first introduced in 2014, 'had been defunct for nine years' before the board voted to revive it in 2023.

angles.claim: NOC collects a dedicated 0.5 percent levy on petroleum sales to build a 'Price Stabilization Fund' explicitly designed to be drawn down during exactly this kind of supply-price shock — but none of the September 30 stories on the freeze (Setopati, Nepal Press, OnlineKhabar) mention whether this fund was tapped, what its current balance is, or why NOC is booking a straight Rs 3.2 billion loss instead.
angles.why_it_matters: Readers are told NOC is 'absorbing' a loss out of goodwill before Dashain, but if a fund built for this purpose already exists, the real story may be about whether that fund is empty, mismanaged, or simply unused — a public-finance question none of the coverage asks.

evidence.fact: Under the 2014 automatic pricing mechanism, 'if petroleum product prices rise, the NOC will draw an amount from the fund to moderate the increased prices,' funded by a 0.5 percent tax NOC levies on petroleum products.
NOC's own statement frames the Rs 3.2 billion figure purely as a 15-day loss tied to floods and Dashain, with no reference to any stabilization fund or reserve being used.

angles.claim: Petroleum pricing in Nepal has historically sat with government officials rather than an independent NOC management: before 2014 the Council of Ministers set prices outright, and as recently as 2023 the NOC board chairman announcing the 'automatic' system was simultaneously the government's Secretary of Commerce and Supply.
angles.why_it_matters: A price freeze timed to the government's biggest festival and announced by a board that includes sitting government officials is a decision the state itself has a direct political interest in — avoiding Dashain-season inflation headlines — which is a different story than a purely commercial call by an independent state enterprise.

evidence.fact: Before 2002 and under the import-parity system through 2014, 'the Council of Ministers used to hold the ultimate authority to decide on petroleum pricing.'

NOC's automatic price system was announced by 'Madhukumar Marasini, Chairman of the NOC's board of directors and Secretary of Commerce and Supply' — the same person holding both the corporate and government role.

angles.claim: NOC has issued similarly large, self-reported fortnightly or weekly loss figures for 'unchanged price' decisions in separate earlier episodes — reported elsewhere as close to Rs 5 billion in one period and close to Rs 2 billion a week in another — with no outlet, including today's, publishing the underlying calculation or reconciling it against NOC's audited accounts.
angles.why_it_matters: A recurring headline figure that changes each time, sourced only to NOC's own statement, cannot be checked by readers and risks being treated as fact simply because it is repeated by multiple outlets citing the same press release.

evidence.fact: A separate earlier NOC price-freeze episode was reported under the headline 'Nepal Oil Corporation Reports Nearly Rs 5 Billion Loss in 15 Days.'
Another earlier episode was reported as NOC facing 'a weekly loss of nearly 2 billion' while keeping prices unchanged.

unanswered.question: Does NOC's Price Stabilization Fund currently hold any balance, and was it used — fully, partly, or not at all — to offset this fortnightly loss instead of booking it as a straight deficit?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Nepal Oil Corporation's finance department or the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, which oversees NOC

unanswered.question: Who currently sits on NOC's board of directors, and does the board still include a sitting government secretary as chairman, as it did in 2023?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Nepal Oil Corporation's public board records or the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies

unanswered.question: How long will the price freeze last, and will NOC recover the foregone revenue through a sharper price correction once Dashain and the flood relief period end?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Nepal Oil Corporation's board or spokesperson

unanswered.question: What is NOC's current total outstanding debt or arrears to Indian Oil Corporation, and how does this Rs 3.2 billion 15-day figure compare with NOC's audited financial statements rather than its own press statement?
unanswered.who_could_answer: NOC's audited annual accounts, the Office of the Auditor General of Nepal, or Indian Oil Corporation

unanswered.question: Were households, transporters or dealers in flood-affected districts like Bhotekoshi consulted or quoted on how the freeze actually helps them, given the decision was announced from Kathmandu citing their situation?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Local district administration offices or transport/dealer associations in the Bhotekoshi/Sindhupalchok flood-affected area

investigation.summary: Every outlet repeated NOC's own Rs 3.2 billion figure and its floods-and-Dashain rationale, but none asked why NOC bypassed the dedicated Price Stabilization Fund it already collects for exactly this kind of shock, or noted that the board has a documented history of overriding its 'automatic' pricing formula in both directions. Nepal Wire can also point out that pricing authority in Nepal has long sat partly with government officials inside NOC's own board, making a festival-timed freeze a decision the state has a direct political stake in, not a purely commercial one.

ranking.reason: Every household and transporter pays this price right before Dashain, and the board decision is confirmed by Setopati, Nepal Press, Ratopati, OnlineKhabar and Khabarhub. The Rs 3.2 billion 15 day loss must be attributed to NOC as its own estimate, and the piece should say NOC has not announced how long the freeze lasts. Weakest reach dimension: share identity.

Confirmed at rank 2. Every household and transporter buys fuel and LPG right before Dashain, and Setopati, Nepal Press, Ratopati, OnlineKhabar and Khabarhub all report the board decision. The Rs 3.2 billion 15 day loss is NOC's own unaudited estimate and must be attributed to NOC. Reach is amended from 70 to 68 because an unchanged price gives readers little to feel. Weakest reach dimension: emotional charge.

findings.passage: NOC's own statement framed Tuesday's Rs 3.2 billion figure as a straight loss, with no mention of whether the fund was drawn on instead.
findings.problem: The investigation treats the March 2026 Kathmandu Post figure of 'nearly Rs 20 billion' as if it still describes the fund's balance in September 2026. In between, Nepal went through a severe Gulf-conflict fuel crisis in March-April 2026 in which NOC itself reported cumulative losses of Rs 18.81 billion by early April and the government cut the work week to cope with fuel shortages. That crisis is exactly the kind of shock the stabilization fund exists for. Presenting a seven-month-old balance as current, with no mention of the intervening crisis that plausibly drew the fund down, makes the central 'what the coverage missed' claim misleading rather than merely incomplete.
findings.suggested_fix: Either confirm the fund's balance as of September 2026 directly with NOC or the Ministry, or add a line noting the March 2026 figure predates the April 2026 Gulf-crisis fuel losses and may no longer reflect the fund's current size.

findings.passage: That discretion cuts both ways: it let a prime minister force a price cut in 2023, and it lets the board freeze prices for Dashain now.
findings.problem: Both examples cited are the same direction: both block a price increase the formula called for (the 2023 cooking gas rollback cancelled a rise; the 2026 freeze blocks a rise). Neither shows the mechanism being overridden to withhold a price decrease from customers, which is the actual 'other direction' and which the newsroom's own investigation found evidence for (NOC blocking a Rs 27.44 LPG price cut in March 2024) but did not include in the article. The 'cuts both ways' claim is therefore not supported by the two examples the body actually gives.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add the 2024 example of NOC refusing to pass on a cooking gas price cut, which is the genuine 'other direction,' or rewrite the sentence to say the mechanism has twice been overridden to prevent consumers from facing price rises, without claiming it cuts both ways.

findings.passage: Nepal Oil Corporation Holds Fuel Prices Steady, Books Rs 3.2 Billion Loss
findings.problem: The headline states the Rs 3.2 billion loss as settled fact in the newsroom's own voice. The article's own 'what we still do not know' section admits this figure has not been checked against audited accounts and comes only from NOC's press statement. 'Books' implies a formal accounting entry, which has not been verified.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to 'NOC Says It Will Lose Rs 3.2 Billion' or similar, attributing the estimate to NOC rather than stating it as a booked fact.

findings.passage: NOC says the 15-day freeze before Dashain will cost it Rs 3.2 billion, but it has not said if its own rainy-day fund was tapped.
findings.problem: Calling it 'the 15-day freeze' implies a fixed, known duration, but the article's own 'what we still do not know' section says 'How long the freeze will last' is unconfirmed. The 15 days refers to the standard pricing review cycle NOC used to calculate the loss estimate, not a stated end date for the freeze.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as 'NOC says the freeze, which it costed over the standard 15-day pricing cycle, will cost it Rs 3.2 billion' or similar, to avoid implying the freeze itself has a known 15-day duration.

findings.passage: As of March 2026, NOC spokesperson Thakur told the Kathmandu Post the fund held "nearly Rs 20 billion,"
findings.problem: The 2023 Kathmandu Post source quoted earlier in the same article identifies Manoj Kumar Thakur as NOC's 'deputy director,' not 'spokesperson.' Using two different titles for the same named official in one piece is an inconsistency readers and the official himself could flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same, verified title for Thakur throughout, confirming whether his March 2026 role was deputy director or spokesperson before publishing.

findings.passage: If NOC's board can freeze prices for a festival, should it also explain, in public, exactly how much of its rainy day fund it used first?
findings.problem: The trigger question assumes as fact that NOC used the fund ('how much... it used'), when the body explicitly states NOC has not said whether the fund was tapped at all. This frames an unconfirmed premise as settled, which the house style bars: a trigger must rest on the record, not an assumption no source carries.
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase to ask whether NOC used the fund at all, e.g. 'Should NOC have to say in public whether it used its rainy day fund before booking this as a straight loss?'

findings.problem: The sources list cites Ekantipur's reporting through a Google News redirect URL rather than Ekantipur's own published article address. House style and the newsroom rules call for the original outlet's own URL over an aggregator link, both for verifiability and to credit the outlet correctly.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the Google News redirect with Ekantipur's direct article URL before publication.

findings.passage:
NOC FREEZES FUEL PRICES
NOT AUTOMATIC SINCE 2023
findings.problem: House style calls for two lines of five to six words on the card headline. Both lines here run only four words each, below the specified range.
findings.suggested_fix: Expand each line slightly to hit five or six words while staying under 24 characters, e.g. 'NOC HOLDS FUEL PRICES DOWN' / 'FORMULA NOT AUTOMATIC SINCE 2023' and recount characters.

findings.passage: NOC's own published board list names the government's Secretary of Commerce and Supplies as the corporation's board chairman, a structure that has held since at least 2023
findings.problem: Nepal appears to have gone through major political upheaval between the 2023 reference point and this October 2026 article, including a change of prime minister, which the piece never mentions or accounts for. Stating the arrangement 'has held since at least 2023' without naming who currently occupies the Secretary and chairman roles, or noting any change of government in between, leaves readers unable to judge whether the accountability point still applies to the people currently in charge.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the current Secretary of Commerce and Supplies/board chairman as of September 2026, not just the 2023 reference, and note if the government has changed since then.

findings.passage: Your petrol price did not rise this week only because Nepal Oil Corporation chose to absorb a Rs 3.2 billion hit instead of passing India's hike to you before Dashain.
findings.problem: The word 'only' overstates certainty about motive. NOC cited floods and Dashain as its reasons, per OnlineKhabar, but the social hook asserts a single causal explanation ('only because') the sources do not establish as exclusive, since the board's discretion and political timing are also live factors the piece itself raises.
findings.suggested_fix: Soften to 'because NOC chose to absorb a Rs 3.2 billion hit rather than pass India's hike to you before Dashain,' dropping 'only' so the hook does not claim a single, exclusive motive.

red_team.summary: The piece does real, source-traceable investigative work on NOC's pricing discretion and the unexplained stabilization fund, but its two strongest claims have cracks: the 'cuts both ways' line is not actually supported by the two examples given, and the headline fund figure of 'nearly Rs 20 billion' is presented as current when it predates a major Gulf-conflict fuel crisis the piece never mentions. The headline states an unaudited loss estimate as settled fact, and the caption's trigger assumes a fact the body says is unconfirmed. Fix the stale fund figure, the illogical 'cuts both ways' framing, and the overstated headline and trigger before publication; the rest of the piece is well sourced and genuinely useful to readers before Dashain.

responses.response: The red team is right. The March 2026 fund balance predates the April 2026 Gulf-crisis fuel losses NOC itself reported, so presenting it as describing the fund's current size is misleading, not just dated. The 'what the coverage missed' claim needs that caveat or fresh confirmation.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: 'As of March 2026, before the Gulf-crisis fuel losses that followed in April, NOC spokesperson Thakur told the Kathmandu Post the fund held "nearly Rs 20 billion." NOC reported cumulative losses of Rs 18.81 billion by early April during that crisis, and has not said what the fund's balance is now or whether this freeze drew on it.' Add the Clickmandu URL to sources.

responses.response: Correct. Both cited examples are the mechanism being overridden to block a price rise, not one blocking a rise and one blocking a fall. 'Cuts both ways' is not supported by the two examples given and the piece should either add the genuine opposite example or drop the claim.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace with: 'That discretion has now been used twice to block price rises the formula would have required: once in 2023, when a prime minister ordered a cooking gas rollback, and now, for Dashain.' If the 2024 LPG price cut example can be verified, add it as the genuine other-direction case instead.

responses.response: Fair catch. 'Books' implies an audited accounting entry, but the figure is NOC's own press estimate, which the article's own unanswered-questions section acknowledges has not been checked against audited accounts.
responses.proposed_edit: Change headline to: 'Nepal Oil Corporation Holds Fuel Prices Steady, Says It Will Lose Rs 3.2 Billion'

responses.response: The piece itself flags 'how long the freeze will last' as unknown, which sits awkwardly against the dek's 'the 15-day freeze.' The 15 days is NOC's costing window, not a stated end date for the price freeze, so the dek should not imply a fixed duration.
responses.proposed_edit: Change dek to: 'NOC says the freeze, costed over its standard 15-day pricing cycle, will cost it Rs 3.2 billion, but it has not said if its own rainy-day fund was tapped.'

responses.response: Using 'deputy director' in one reference and 'spokesperson' in another for the same named official, without noting a role change, is an inconsistency that should be resolved or flagged before publication.
responses.proposed_edit: Verify Thakur's title as of March 2026 directly from the Kathmandu Post piece and use one consistent title throughout, or add a clause noting he held both the deputy director and spokesperson role if that is confirmed.

responses.response: The trigger says 'how much of its rainy day fund it used,' which presumes the fund was tapped. The body is explicit that NOC has not said whether the fund was used at all. That is a real contradiction the house style bars.
responses.proposed_edit: Change trigger to: 'Should NOC have to say in public whether it used its rainy day fund at all before booking this as a straight loss?'

responses.response: House style prefers the original outlet's own URL over an aggregator link. The Google News redirect should be swapped for Ekantipur's direct article address before publication.
responses.proposed_edit: Locate and substitute Ekantipur's own published URL for the September 30 report in place of the Google News redirect link.

responses.response: Counting the words, both lines run four words, short of the five to six word range the style guide sets for the card headline.
responses.proposed_edit: Revise to two lines of five to six words each, under 24 characters, e.g. 'NOC HOLDS FUEL PRICES DOWN' and 'FORMULA NOT AUTOMATIC SINCE 2023', checking character counts before use.

responses.response: Checked independently: Nepal has in fact changed governments twice since the 2023 reference point, through an interim premiership and a new prime minister in 2026. The article names only the 2023 chairman and office structure without confirming who holds the Commerce and Supplies Secretary role now or flagging the change of government, which the zero-knowledge test and completeness rule both require.
responses.proposed_edit: Add the name of the current Secretary of Commerce and Supplies and NOC board chairman as of September 2026, and a line noting the government has changed since the 2023 reference, e.g. 'Nepal has since had an interim government and a new prime minister, but NOC's own board list still shows the same chairman structure as of [date].'

responses.response: The hook's 'only because' refers to the mechanism, not an exhaustive list of NOC's motives. It says the price stayed flat only because NOC chose to absorb the hike rather than pass it on, which is mechanically true regardless of why NOC made that choice. The article separately reports NOC's stated reasons (floods, Dashain) in the body, so there is no conflict between the hook's claim about the pricing mechanism and the body's account of motive.
responses.proposed_edit: No change needed. Optionally soften to 'because NOC chose to absorb a Rs 3.2 billion hit rather than pass India's hike to you before Dashain' if the editor wants to preempt the misreading, but the current wording is not inaccurate.

defense.summary: Six of ten findings point to real problems: a stale fund balance presented as current (f1), an unsupported 'cuts both ways' framing (f2), a headline that states an unverified loss as settled fact (f3), a dek implying a fixed freeze duration the body says is unknown (f4), an inconsistent title for the same official (f5), and a trigger question that assumes the fund was tapped when the body says that is unconfirmed (f6). Two formatting issues are also valid: an aggregator URL instead of the original outlet's link (f7) and a card headline short of the required word count (f8). An independent check confirmed f9's underlying premise, Nepal has changed governments twice since 2023, so the piece should name the current officeholder and note the political change rather than relying on a 2023 reference. Only f10 is defensible as written: the social hook's 'only because' describes the pricing mechanism, not an exhaustive claim about NOC's motives, and does not conflict with the body's separate account of NOC's stated reasons.

rulings.note: High severity. The body, take and caption present a March 4, 2026 balance as if it were current. That figure predates the Gulf crisis fuel losses Clickmandu reported by early April. Fix with a dated caveat, not with any claim that the fund was drawn down, which no source states.

Both examples block a price rise, so 'cuts both ways' is unsupported. 'Force a price cut' also misstates a rollback of a rise. Use the defence's rewrite. Do not add the 2024 LPG example unless the editor reads it in the Kathmandu Post article itself.
'Books' turns NOC's own estimate into an accounting fact in the newsroom's voice. Attribute the figure to NOC.
The 15 days is NOC's costing window per Nepal Press, not a stated freeze length. The body itself lists duration as unknown.
Give Thakur the title each Kathmandu Post article used, dated to that article, so the change reads as a role at a time and not as an error.

The trigger presumes the fund was used. The defence's replacement reintroduces 'booking', the f3 problem, and nearly every reader would answer it yes, so it fails the ninety percent test. A side picking question is ordered below.
The rules prefer the original outlet over an aggregator. Ekantipur also anchors a negative claim about what it did not report, so its own URL must be checkable.

Both card lines run four words. The card also states 'NOT AUTOMATIC SINCE 2023' flat as a continuing fact. The only source is a November 2023 quote, so the record does not carry status through 2026. The defence's example line is 32 characters and breaks the 24 character cap. A replacement is ordered.

Sustained narrowly. Name the chairman the NOC board page lists now, with role, per the first mention rule. Do not add the defence's line on an interim government and a new prime minister. No source in the list carries it.

As the defence argues, 'only because' describes the mechanism. The pump price held because NOC chose not to pass the rise on, which the record shows. The hook does need the record's qualifier 'estimated' on the Rs 3.2 billion, ordered below.

required_edits: DATE, everywhere: September 30, 2026 was a Wednesday, not a Tuesday. In body paragraph 1 change 'on Tuesday, September 30' to 'on Wednesday, September 30'.
